sources.entry: docker-mailserver - Production-ready fullstack but simple mail server (SMTP, IMAP, LDAP, Antispam, Antivirus, etc.) running inside a container. Only configuration files, no SQL database. (Source Code) MIT Docker
docker-mailserver | Production-ready mail server (SMTP, IMAP, antispam) in a single container

summary.one_liner: A production-ready, fullstack containerized mail server (SMTP, IMAP, POP3, antispam, antivirus) that is configured through files rather than a SQL database.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a single-container mail server bundling Postfix for SMTP with SMTP or LDAP authentication, and Dovecot for IMAP, POP3, SASL, LDAP, basic Sieve and quotas. Spam and virus filtering is covered by Rspamd, Amavis, SpamAssassin (with custom rules) and ClamAV with automatic updates. Mail authentication and anti-abuse components include OpenDKIM, OpenDMARC, Fail2ban, Postscreen and Postgrey. It can fetch mail from other accounts via Fetchmail and Getmail6, supports LetsEncrypt, manual and self-signed certificates, and offers OAuth2 via XOAUTH2 or OAUTHBEARER SASL mechanisms. A setup script is provided for configuration and maintenance.
use_cases: run my own email server for a domain
filter spam and viruses on incoming mail
set up DKIM and DMARC for outgoing mail
host company email with LDAP logins
collect mail from external accounts with Fetchmail or Getmail6
notable: Entire mail stack runs in one container, configured with plain files and no SQL database
Covers both SMTP/IMAP sending and receiving plus antispam, antivirus and DKIM/DMARC
Supports LDAP authentication through Postfix, Dovecot and SASLauthd
Includes OAuth2 authentication via XOAUTH2 or OAUTHBEARER SASL
Documentation is versioned; the README asks users to read docs matching their image version
caveats: Maintained by volunteers since January 2021 after originally being created by @tomav
Issue tracker is for bugs, not personal support; users are directed to the documentation first
Setup requires mail-server knowledge (DNS records, certificates) that the README points to external docs for
